notesStmt.note: A note at the bottom of the manuscript states that it was "sent to Herald March 11," indicating the draft was likely completed in early 1888, just before the time of publication. It seems likely that the first and third leaf of this manuscript were at one time pasted to the second leaf, with the first leaf covering the first stanza on the second leaf, leaving just the second stanza and thus creating a complete draft of the poem.

This manuscript contains a draft version of the poem "The Wallabout Martyrs," which was first published in the New York Herald, March 16, 1888. The poem was then included in November Boughs (1888), as well as the deathbed edition of Leaves of Grass (1891–92).

lg.head: The Wallabout Martyrs
lg.note: [In Brooklyn in an old vault lie huddled at this moment the undoubtedly authentic remains of many thousand of the staunchest and earliest ‸Revolutionary patriots, from the British prison-ships and prisons of the Revolutionary times of 1776⹀'83 in and around New York; originally buried‸—many thousands of them—in trenches in the Wallabout sands.]

lg.l:
Greater by far to thee than
tomb of Alexander,

More, more than memory of
Achilles and Ulysses,

Greater than memory of Achilles
or Ulysses,

More, more by far to thee than
tomb of Alexander,

SomeThose cart loads of ‸old ‸charnel ashes dust, mould, scales
and splints of bones,

Once living men—once resolute
courage, aspiration, strength
The stepping⹀stones to thee to-day ‸and here America.
